Hmm, let me look at this hand carefully. I've got:
- 2 Forests (lands)
- 2 Talisman of Impulse (2-mana artifacts for ramp)
- Malevolent Rumble (2-mana spell)
- Icetill Explorer (4-mana 2/4 creature)
- Emrakul, the Promised End (13-mana bomb)

This is a 7-card hand with only 2 lands. While I have ramp pieces (the Talismans), I need 2 mana to cast them first, which means I need to hit my land drops. With only 2 lands in a 7-card hand, this is risky - I could easily miss land drops and get stuck.

However, if I mulligan to 6, I'm not guaranteed a better hand. Let me think about the curve:
- Turn 1: Forest, pass
- Turn 2: Forest, Talisman (if I draw a land, I can cast the other Talisman or Rumble)
- Turn 3+: Need more lands to function

This hand has some play to it if I draw lands, but it's land-light. In the old days, we'd keep marginal hands and like it! But competitively, 2 lands with no card draw in the opener is concerning.

Actually, wait - I should keep this. I have two 2-mana ramp pieces, so if I draw even one more land in my first few draws, I can start deploying my Talismans and potentially curve out. The hand has a plan and payoffs.

annotations.description: With Sire of Seven Deaths (7 mana, colorless Eldrazi) and Emrakul in hand, Ugin's Labyrinth would have been significantly better. Ugin's Labyrinth can imprint a colorless card with mana value 7+ (like Sire of Seven Deaths or Emrakul) to produce 2 colorless mana per tap, effectively acting as a Sol land. The player already has multiple colorless Eldrazi to imprint. Eldrazi Temple only produces 2 colorless mana specifically for Eldrazi spells/abilities, while Ugin's Labyrinth does the same with imprint but is a land that can be played immediately and doesn't have the Eldrazi-only restriction on the bonus mana. More importantly, the player put TWO copies of Ugin's Labyrinth into the graveyard by not picking one, losing access to both. With Icetill Explorer in hand (which lets you play lands from graveyard), one copy could potentially be recovered, but having it in hand is still better. Ugin's Labyrinth with imprint would have provided faster acceleration toward casting Emrakul or Sire.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Eldrazi Temple over Ugin's Labyrinth from Malevolent Rumble's revealed cards.
annotations.betterLine: Select Ugin's Labyrinth, which when played can imprint Sire of Seven Deaths or Emrakul to produce 2 colorless mana per tap — equally good or better acceleration for the Eldrazi game plan, while preserving the second Ugin's Labyrinth in graveyard for potential recovery with Icetill Explorer.

annotations.description: Took Sire of Seven Deaths instead of Emrakul, the Promised End with Thoughtseize. Emrakul's cast trigger (controlling opponent's next turn) is essentially game-ending, and taking Sire puts a creature card type in the graveyard, reducing Emrakul's cost from 9 to 8. The opponent has Icetill Explorer enabling land replay from graveyard (including 2x Ugin's Labyrinth which can imprint Emrakul for massive mana), making casting Emrakul very realistic.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to discard Sire of Seven Deaths
annotations.betterLine: Discard Emrakul, the Promised End - it's the most powerful and game-warping threat, its cast trigger is nearly unbeatable, and leaving it in hand while reducing its cost by discarding Sire is counterproductive.

annotations.description: GLM47 Coach passed the turn with 3 mana available (Steam Vents + Polluted Delta for a land) and multiple playable cards. Gran-Gran costs {U} and could have been cast off Steam Vents, providing a body that loots when tapped and potentially enables cost reduction later. The opponent has an Icetill Explorer (2/4) that is generating value through land-from-graveyard and mill, and a Sire of Seven Deaths in the graveyard that could be reanimated or recast. Developing the board with Gran-Gran would help find answers and apply pressure. Additionally, Faithless Looting could have been cast to improve hand quality and stock the graveyard for Persist (which could target the opponent's Sire of Seven Deaths from their graveyard - though Persist only works on your own graveyard). At minimum, casting Gran-Gran for {U} to develop the board was free and had no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting any spells, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Gran-Gran for {U} off Steam Vents to develop the board and enable future looting triggers. Could also consider casting Faithless Looting to improve hand quality and fill graveyard.

annotations.description: Casting Emperor of Bones before combat is suboptimal sequencing. Emperor of Bones has an 'at the beginning of combat on your turn' trigger that exiles a card from a graveyard, which won't trigger this turn since the precombat main phase hasn't moved to combat yet — wait, actually the combat trigger will still happen this turn since it triggers at the beginning of combat. However, casting a creature before combat when holding Fatal Push and Bitter Triumph (trick-style cards) gives the opponent information unnecessarily. More importantly, the player should consider sequencing: they have Polluted Delta uncracked, and should likely crack it first to enable Revolt for Fatal Push (which could kill Icetill Explorer, a 2/4 with mana value 4). Playing Emperor of Bones before cracking Polluted Delta means if they need Fatal Push with Revolt later this turn, they've used mana on the creature first. Additionally, Faithless Looting could be cast first to improve hand quality and potentially set up better plays, since Emperor of Bones wants good targets in graveyards to reanimate.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emperor of Bones as the first action in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Crack Polluted Delta first to enable Revolt for Fatal Push, then consider casting Faithless Looting to filter the hand (discarding cards like Persist or extra Gran-Grans), before deciding whether to deploy Emperor of Bones or hold up removal mana.

annotations.description: Should play a land from graveyard first (via Icetill Explorer) before casting Sowing Mycospawn. Playing Eldrazi Temple from graveyard would add extra mana and trigger landfall/mill, potentially enabling additional plays this turn (like also casting Talisman of Impulse). Land drops should come before spell casting for maximum mana efficiency.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sowing Mycospawn before playing a land from graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Play Eldrazi Temple (or Ugin's Labyrinth) from graveyard first via Icetill Explorer's ability, trigger landfall mill, then cast Sowing Mycospawn with more mana available for the same turn

annotations.description: Casting Bitter Triumph in response to their own Faithless Looting means they must discard a card (or pay 3 life) before seeing the 2 cards Faithless Looting would draw. By letting Looting resolve first, they'd have 2 additional cards to choose from as discard fodder for both Bitter Triumph and Looting's discard, maximizing card selection.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bitter Triumph before Faithless Looting resolved, requiring an immediate discard from the current hand.
annotations.betterLine: Let Faithless Looting resolve first (draw 2, discard 2), then cast Bitter Triumph on Icetill Explorer, discarding the worst remaining card. This maximizes card quality across both discard effects.

annotations.description: Discarded Psychic Frog (a premier win condition and card advantage engine) instead of one of the two duplicate Gran-Grans in hand. Gran-Gran without Lessons in graveyard is just a 1/2 looter, and having two copies makes one very expendable. Psychic Frog is significantly more impactful as a threat that can grow, gain flying, and draw cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Psychic Frog as the additional cost for Bitter Triumph
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Gran-Gran copies instead, preserving the more powerful Psychic Frog as a win condition

annotations.description: Discarding Fatal Push over a second copy of Gran-Gran is debatable. Fatal Push is premium removal that could deal with future threats, while having two Gran-Gran in hand is redundant (legendary creature). Against an Eldrazi ramp deck, Fatal Push may not line up perfectly with their biggest threats, but it still has value against Sowing Mycospawn (MV 4 with revolt) or other mid-sized creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Swamp and Fatal Push, keeping Persist, two Gran-Gran, and Undercity Sewers.
annotations.betterLine: Discard one Gran-Gran (legendary, redundant copy) and Swamp, keeping Fatal Push for interaction alongside Persist, Gran-Gran, and Undercity Sewers.

annotations.description: Exiled Psychic Frog (1/2) with Emperor of Bones instead of Devourer of Destiny (6/6) from opponent's graveyard. When Emperor of Bones adapts and reanimates the exiled creature, a 6/6 hasty attacker is far more impactful than a 1/2 Psychic Frog (which would need hand cards discarded to pump and gets sacrificed at end step regardless). This also has the secondary benefit of denying the opponent a powerful card from their graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Psychic Frog from own graveyard with Emperor of Bones' combat trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Devourer of Destiny from opponent's graveyard - it's a 6/6 that would deal massive damage when reanimated with haste via Adapt, and denies the opponent access to it

annotations.description: Sonnet Gramps had enough mana to cast Sowing Mycospawn with kicker but chose to cast it unkicked. With Forest+Utopia Sprawl (GG), Forest (G), Stomping Ground (G/R), Eldrazi Temple (CC for colorless Eldrazi), and Eldrazi Spawn (C), they had at least 7 mana available, more than enough for the kicked cost of {3}{G}{1}{C} (6 total). Kicking it would exile one of the opponent's three lands, which would be devastating against an opponent at only 3 lands with Emperor of Bones as their only threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sowing Mycospawn without kicker, only getting the land search effect.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sowing Mycospawn with kicker using Eldrazi Temple's CC (Mycospawn is devoid/colorless Eldrazi) plus other mana sources, searching for a land AND exiling one of the opponent's three lands to cripple their mana development.

annotations.description: Bojuka Bog enters tapped, preventing Emrakul from being cast this turn. With 5 card types in graveyard (land, instant/kindred, sorcery, artifact, creature), Emrakul costs 8. Current mana production is 7 (Forest+Sprawl=2, Forest=1, Stomping Ground=1, Eldrazi Temple=2 for Eldrazi, Spawn=1). Playing Verdant Catacombs (fetching untapped) or Sanctum of Ugin would provide the 8th mana needed to cast Emrakul this turn, gaining control of the opponent's next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Bojuka Bog, which enters tapped, to exile opponent's graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Play Verdant Catacombs (or Sanctum of Ugin) to have 8 mana available and cast Emrakul, the Promised End this turn. Sanctum of Ugin would be best as it also triggers to tutor another colorless creature when Emrakul is cast. Exiling opponent's graveyard with Bojuka Bog provides marginal value compared to casting a 13/13 and taking control of opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Chose to reanimate Psychic Frog (1/2) instead of Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 with first strike, menace, trample, lifelink, haste). Sire would have been nearly unblockable with menace (opponent only has Sowing Mycospawn and an Eldrazi Spawn token), would deal significant trample damage, and gain 7 life with lifelink. The creature gets sacrificed at end of turn regardless, so maximum immediate impact is what matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Psychic Frog (1/2) onto the battlefield with Emperor of Bones trigger
annotations.betterLine: Put Sire of Seven Deaths onto the battlefield - it attacks as a 7/7 haste menace trample lifelink creature, likely dealing 7 damage (or at minimum 3+ trample damage through blocks) while gaining 7 life, a massive swing compared to a 1/2 Psychic Frog

annotations.description: Discarded a land (Undercity Sewers) when at only 3 lands on board, rather than discarding one of two copies of the legendary Gran-Gran. With only 3 lands, the 4th land drop is important for deploying threats and casting spells. Since Gran-Gran is legendary, the second copy has significantly reduced value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Undercity Sewers to Psychic Frog's pump ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Gran-Gran copies instead, preserving the land drop to develop mana while discarding a card with diminished value due to the legendary rule

annotations.description: Gran-Gran has 'Whenever Gran-Gran becomes tapped, draw a card, then discard a card.' Attacking with Gran-Gran provides a free loot trigger. The opponent's only meaningful blocker is Sowing Mycospawn (3/3), which they're unlikely to use on a 1/2. The Eldrazi Spawn (0/1) could chump but that's a fine trade. The player also has a duplicate Gran-Gran in hand, reducing the risk of losing it.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Emperor of Bones, leaving Gran-Gran back
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Emperor of Bones and Gran-Gran to get a free loot trigger from Gran-Gran's tap ability, filtering through the hand which contains a duplicate Gran-Gran

annotations.description: Sonnet Gramps chose not to block Emperor of Bones (4/4) with the Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1), which would have absorbed no damage but could have chumped to save 4 life. At 17 life going to 13, this matters because the opponent has an aggressive deck. The Eldrazi Spawn token provides {C} when sacrificed, but with Emrakul in hand and a developing board, saving 4 life by chump blocking with a 0/1 token that provides only 1 colorless mana seems like the better trade. The mana from the spawn is relatively minor compared to 4 life points.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block Emperor of Bones, taking 4 damage (17 -> 13 life)
annotations.betterLine: Chump block with Eldrazi Spawn Token to preserve 4 life points. The token's sacrifice ability for {C} is worth less than 4 life in most scenarios, especially against an aggressive opponent.

annotations.description: Gran-Gran is a legendary creature, and GLM47 Coach already has a Gran-Gran on the battlefield. Casting a second Gran-Gran will cause the legend rule to apply, forcing the player to sacrifice one of the two copies. This wastes a card for essentially no benefit - at best, they get a single loot trigger from the new Gran-Gran becoming tapped (but it was just cast, so it won't tap unless they have a way to tap it). Meanwhile, they have Psychic Frog available to cast, which would be a much more impactful play as a 1/2 that can grow, gain flying, and draw cards on combat damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a second Gran-Gran while one was already on the battlefield, triggering the legend rule and wasting a card.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Psychic Frog for UB, which provides a growing threat with evasion potential and card advantage, without wasting a card to the legend rule.

annotations.description: Discarded Persist instead of the duplicate legendary Gran-Gran. The second Gran-Gran cannot be cast while the first is on the battlefield (legend rule would immediately kill one). Persist at least has future potential if creatures die - Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog could become valid targets later.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Persist to Psychic Frog's ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard the duplicate Gran-Gran, which is completely dead while the battlefield copy survives, keeping Persist for potential future reanimation targets

annotations.description: Not attacking with Gran-Gran means missing a free loot trigger (draw + discard) since Gran-Gran draws a card when it becomes tapped. With 0 cards in hand, this card filtering is very valuable. Psychic Frog could also potentially sneak in for damage and a card draw if unblocked.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Emperor of Bones, leaving Gran-Gran and Psychic Frog back
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (or at minimum Gran-Gran alongside Emperor of Bones) to get the free loot trigger from Gran-Gran tapping and potentially sneak damage through with Psychic Frog

annotations.description: At 9 life against a board with Psychic Frog (which can pump and gain flying), declining to block Emperor of Bones drops to 5 life, putting them in lethal range. The Eldrazi Spawn token could chump block to save 4 life at minimal cost (sacrificing a 0/1 token), though preserving it for Emrakul mana is a consideration.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 4 damage to go to 5 life
annotations.betterLine: Chump block with Eldrazi Spawn Token to stay at 9 life, reducing vulnerability to Psychic Frog attacks. While the Spawn provides mana for Emrakul, surviving is more important.

annotations.description: Playing Eldrazi Temple instead of Sanctum of Ugin when both provide enough mana to cast the discounted Emrakul this turn. Sanctum of Ugin would trigger on casting Emrakul (colorless spell with MV 7+), allowing a sacrifice to tutor for another colorless creature, providing significant card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Eldrazi Temple as their land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Sanctum of Ugin instead. With Forest, Forest+Utopia Sprawl, Eldrazi Temple (2 colorless for Eldrazi), Stomping Ground, Bojuka Bog, Sanctum (1 colorless), and Eldrazi Spawn token (1 colorless), there's still enough mana to cast the 7-cost Emrakul, and Sanctum's trigger would let you tutor for another colorless creature.

annotations.description: Emrakul, the Promised End costs 7 mana (13 minus 6 card types in graveyard: land, instant, sorcery, artifact, creature, kindred). With Forest+Utopia Sprawl (2), Forest (1), Eldrazi Temple (2 for Eldrazi), Stomping Ground (1), Bojuka Bog (1), and Eldrazi Spawn sacrifice (1) = 8 mana available, Emrakul could be cast this turn while the opponent is completely tapped out. Emrakul's mind control trigger plus a 13/13 flying trampler would likely win the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Icetill Explorer, a 2/4 creature for 4 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Emrakul, the Promised End for 7 mana, gaining control of the opponent's next turn and deploying a 13/13 flying trampler while the opponent is tapped out with no way to interact

annotations.description: Exiled Persist (a sorcery) with Emperor of Bones instead of Abhorrent Oculus (a 5/5 flying creature). Emperor of Bones can only reanimate creature cards exiled with it, so exiling Persist accomplishes nothing. With Abhorrent Oculus exiled, they could adapt Emperor of Bones for {1}{B} (mana available from untapped lands), putting a 4/4 flying Oculus onto the battlefield with haste. Combined with potentially pumping Psychic Frog by discarding the Psychic Frog from hand, they could attack for significant flying damage against an opponent at 9 life. Instead they skipped attacks entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Persist (a sorcery) with Emperor of Bones, then skipped attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Abhorrent Oculus with Emperor of Bones, then pay {1}{B} to adapt Emperor (getting +1/+1 counters), which puts Abhorrent Oculus onto the battlefield as a 4/4 flyer with haste. Discard Psychic Frog from hand to pump battlefield Psychic Frog to 2/3 and give it flying. Attack with both flyers for 6 damage, putting opponent to 3 life.

annotations.description: At 9 life facing Emperor of Bones, Gran-Gran, and Psychic Frog, casting Talisman of Impulse for ramp is lower priority than addressing the board. Additionally, land should be played before casting spells - Sanctum of Ugin is particularly valuable as it synergizes with casting Emrakul later. Kozilek's Return would clear all three opposing creatures (all have 2 or less toughness) and set up the graveyard trigger for later Emrakul cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Talisman of Impulse for incremental ramp
annotations.betterLine: Play Sanctum of Ugin (or Verdant Catacombs) as land drop first, then consider casting Kozilek's Return to clear Emperor of Bones, Gran-Gran, and Psychic Frog, protecting the 9 life total while also putting Kozilek's Return in graveyard for its Emrakul-triggered 5-damage ability later.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones can only reanimate creature cards exiled with it when it gets +1/+1 counters via Adapt. Exiling Malevolent Rumble (a sorcery) means Emperor of Bones cannot reanimate anything. Abhorrent Oculus (5/5 flyer) was available in their own graveyard and could have been exiled, then reanimated with haste by paying {1}{B} for Adapt 2. With opponent at 9 life, a 5/5 flying haste attacker alongside existing creatures could threaten lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Malevolent Rumble (a sorcery) from opponent's graveyard with Emperor of Bones trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Abhorrent Oculus from own graveyard, then use Adapt 2 ({1}{B}) on Emperor of Bones to reanimate it as a 5/5 flying haste creature for a massive attack with opponent at 9 life

annotations.description: Discarded the second Psychic Frog to pump the battlefield Frog, when Faithless Looting was also in hand. Faithless Looting has flashback ({2}{R}), so discarding it loses almost nothing since it can still be cast from the graveyard. The second Psychic Frog is a real backup threat/additional attacker that is permanently lost by discarding it.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Psychic Frog from hand to put a +1/+1 counter on the battlefield Psychic Frog
annotations.betterLine: Discard Faithless Looting instead to pump Psychic Frog - Faithless Looting retains its flashback value from the graveyard, while preserving the second Psychic Frog as a future threat

annotations.description: Attacking Emperor of Bones into Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) risks losing a valuable creature that provides graveyard interaction and reanimation. Opponent is at 9 life, so 4 total damage isn't close to lethal, and losing Emperor of Bones to a bad trade weakens the board significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all three creatures including Emperor of Bones into a board with Sowing Mycospawn 3/3
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Gran-Gran (for the draw/discard trigger) and Psychic Frog (for potential card draw on damage), keeping Emperor of Bones back as a blocker against the 3/3 Mycospawn and preserving its graveyard exile and reanimation abilities.

annotations.description: Only blocking Emperor of Bones with Icetill Explorer leaves Sonnet Gramps at 2 life (taking 7 from unblocked Psychic Frog + Gran-Gran). At 2 life they're extremely vulnerable to any incidental damage. Sowing Mycospawn could have also blocked Psychic Frog to preserve 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked only Emperor of Bones with Icetill Explorer, going to 2 life
annotations.betterLine: Block Emperor of Bones with Icetill Explorer AND Psychic Frog with Sowing Mycospawn. This preserves 6 life (going to 8 instead of 2), which is far more important than preserving a 3/3 body when at such a low life total facing aggressive creatures.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones is the more dangerous threat on the opponent's board - it can exile creatures from Sonnet Gramps' graveyard (including Icetill Explorer) and reanimate them with haste, plus it can adapt to grow. Gran-Gran is just a 1/2 that loots when tapped. Blocking the lesser threat leaves the more impactful creature alive.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Gran-Gran (1/2 value engine) instead of Emperor of Bones (2/2 recursive reanimator)
annotations.betterLine: Block Emperor of Bones to kill the more dangerous recursive threat that can exploit graveyard creatures

annotations.description: Kozilek's Return would deal 2 damage to all creatures, killing Emperor of Bones (2/2), Gran-Gran (1/2), and possibly Psychic Frog, while keeping Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) alive. Additionally, putting Kozilek's Return in the graveyard sets up its powerful second ability with Emrakul, the Promised End in hand - when Emrakul is cast, Kozilek's Return can be exiled from graveyard to deal 5 damage to all creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with Sowing Mycospawn, trading the 3/3 body for one attacker while still taking damage from the others
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Return to deal 2 damage to all creatures, clearing multiple attackers while preserving Sowing Mycospawn, and putting Kozilek's Return in the graveyard for its Emrakul synergy

annotations.description: Sonnet Gramps is at 3 life with only Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) to block. GLM47 Coach has Psychic Frog (1/2), Emperor of Bones (2/2), and Gran-Gran (1/2). By discarding one card to pump Psychic Frog to 2/3, then attacking with all three (2+2+1=5 power), Sonnet Gramps can only block one creature. Blocking either 2-power creature lets 2+1=3 through for lethal. Even without pump, if opponent blocks the 2/2, only 2 gets through, but with the pump making two 2-power threats, any single block lets exactly 3 through.
annotations.actionTaken: Skipped the attack phase without attacking, missing lethal on board.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a card to Psychic Frog to give it a +1/+1 counter (making it 2/3), then attack with all three creatures (Psychic Frog, Emperor of Bones, Gran-Gran) for lethal damage since opponent can only block one.

annotations.description: While controlling the opponent's turn via Emrakul, Sonnet Gramps passed without using Psychic Frog's activated ability to exile 3 cards from the opponent's graveyard (which included Abhorrent Oculus, Gran-Gran, Emperor of Bones). Exiling these cards would strip the opponent of powerful reanimation targets and future graveyard synergies at no real cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any of the opponent's abilities
annotations.betterLine: Activate Psychic Frog's 'Exile three cards from your graveyard: gains flying' ability to remove key cards (especially Abhorrent Oculus) from the opponent's graveyard, permanently denying reanimation/recursion targets

annotations.description: During the Emrakul control turn's end step, the player passed without activating any of GLM47 Coach's abilities. Gran-Gran could be tapped to draw/discard (letting the controller choose what to discard), and Psychic Frog could discard cards from their hand to waste resources. These activations would strip the opponent's hand of valuable cards before they get their extra turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any of the opponent's abilities during the Emrakul-controlled end step.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Gran-Gran to force a draw/discard (discarding their best card), then use Psychic Frog to discard remaining cards from the opponent's hand, stripping their resources before they take their extra turn.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life. Abhorrent Oculus (mana value 3) is a legal Unearth target and would enter as a 5/5 flyer - since Unearth puts it onto the battlefield without casting, the 'exile six cards' additional cost doesn't apply. A 5/5 flyer is lethal on its own against an opponent at 3 life with no flying blockers. Instead, Gran-Gran (1/2) was chosen, which provides minimal board impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Gran-Gran (1/2) as Unearth target
annotations.betterLine: Choose Abhorrent Oculus as Unearth target, getting a 5/5 flyer for free, then attack with the flyer for lethal damage against the opponent at 3 life

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life with only Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) as a blocker. By discarding an Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog to make it 2/3, then attacking with all three creatures (Emperor 2/2, Frog 2/3, Gran-Gran 1/2), no matter which creature the opponent blocks with Mycospawn, the remaining two deal at least 3 damage, which is lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Psychic Frog's discard ability during combat
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog to pump it to 2/3, then attack with all three creatures for guaranteed lethal regardless of blocks

annotations.description: Opponent is at 3 life with no creatures on the battlefield. Emperor of Bones (2/2) can Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to become 4/4, and Gran-Gran is a 1/2. Attacking with both deals 5 damage to an empty board, which is lethal against an opponent at 3 life. Instead, the attack was skipped entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Sowing Mycospawn from opponent's graveyard and then skipped the attack phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B} to make it a 4/4, then attack with both Emperor of Bones (4/4) and Gran-Gran (1/2) for 5 total damage against 3 life - lethal with no blockers available.

annotations.description: Kozilek's Return deals 2 damage to EACH CREATURE, not to opponents. It's a board wipe effect, not a burn spell. The player is at 3 life and the opponent is at 2 life, but Kozilek's Return cannot deal damage to players. Casting it kills the opponent's Emperor of Bones and Gran-Gran, but also means Sonnet Gramps paid 1 life from Talisman of Impulse to tap for red mana, going to 2 life themselves. Meanwhile, the opponent at 2 life has no way to be killed by this spell. The player should have looked for an actual way to deal 2 damage to the opponent, or focused on setting up a board state to attack for lethal. With 7 lands in play plus Talisman, they could cast Sowing Mycospawn (which is a creature that could attack next turn) while also developing their board. The Kozilek's Return accomplishes clearing the opponent's creatures but doesn't win the game as the player's reasoning incorrectly assumed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kozilek's Return, believing it deals 2 damage to each opponent, thinking it would kill the opponent at 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sowing Mycospawn to develop a creature threat that could attack for lethal next turn, while also searching for a land. Kozilek's Return could still be cast if needed to clear blockers, but the priority should be establishing a lethal attacker since Kozilek's Return doesn't hit players.

annotations.description: The reasoning for casting Kozilek's Return is fundamentally wrong - it deals damage to creatures only, not players, so it cannot 'finish them off' at 2 life. While killing Emperor of Bones is useful, the player should have played a land first (Forest from hand) before casting spells, following proper sequencing. The misunderstanding of the card suggests the player may have cast it primarily for the wrong reason, though it does have board value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kozilek's Return before playing a land, believing it would deal damage to the opponent at 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first (land before spells), then cast Kozilek's Return to clear Emperor of Bones. Understand that Kozilek's Return only hits creatures and plan accordingly for a different win condition.
